transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, doctor, I appreciate you seeing me. I suppose the main reason I finally decided to make an appointment is... well, it's about my eating habits lately. You see, I work all day doing bookkeeping—lots of numbers, very detail-oriented, you know how it is—and then I've been taking this evening class to keep my skills sharp. By the time that class lets out, I'm just completely wiped out. 

And what's been happening, what really brought me in, is that I'll stop for food on the way back. I always think, oh, I'll just grab a quick bite to tide me over, but I end up getting a full fast-food meal. A burger, fries, the works. And then I'll hit the vending machine and get candy, too. But the thing is, even after all that on the drive, I get home and I just keep going. I'll pull out more snacks from the cupboards and just eat... it's almost like I'm making up for the whole entire day in one sitting. I just sit there eating all this stuff, one thing right after another, and I don't know, it just feels like it's gotten out of my control, which is why I figured I better come talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for the food you've eaten?

Well, doctor... I mean, I don't take any pills or laxatives, and heaven knows I don't have the energy to go running around the block at midnight after my classes. But... well, this is hard to admit. Really hard. You know, I'm a 55-year-old man, I should have my life together, right? I shouldn't be dealing with things like this. But... to answer your question about making myself sick... yes. A few times. 

Not every single time, but a few times after those really bad late-night eating spells, I just get this overwhelming panic. I'll be sitting there in the quiet house, and my stomach is just painfully full from the fast food and the candy and whatever else I pulled out of the pantry, and I start thinking about how I just sit at a desk all day doing payroll and ledgers. I don't burn off anything! My metabolism just isn't what it used to be back in the day. And I get so incredibly scared that all that food is just going to immediately show on me. It absolutely terrifies me, the thought of having to buy bigger pants or having people at the office notice I'm letting myself go. 

So, I have... well, I have gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just go in there, shut the door, and do it because I'm so desperate to get it out of my system before it turns into fat. It's an awful feeling, really shameful, honestly, but in that moment, the fear of all those calories showing on my waistline just completely overrides my common sense. I always tell myself I'll never do it again, but then the whole cycle with the late nights and the stress just repeats itself.
How often do these episodes of overeating happen? Do they occur on a regular basis, like several times a week, or are they less frequent?

Well, let me think about the exact timeline here, because time just sort of blurs together when you're staring at spreadsheets and reconciling accounts all day, you know? My evening classes—it's an advanced data management course, very intensive, lots of complex formulas and things that really drain your mental battery—those started up right around the tail end of the summer. So, if I'm looking at the calendar in my head and really tracing it back, this whole cycle has been going on for about the past three months. 

And as for how often it actually happens... well, the class meets twice a week. Sometimes the second class of the week isn't quite as bad because I know the weekend is right around the corner and I can finally catch up on my sleep. But usually, almost without fail, there is at least one night each week where the stress and the exhaustion just completely peak. So, yes, for these past three months, it's been at least one night a week. 

It's always after that class. I'll just completely lose the battle on the drive home, get all that fast food, come into the dark house, tear through the pantry for whatever else I can find, and then... well, then the panic sets in and I end up in the bathroom doing what I told you. Making myself throw up. I always tell myself at the start of the week, I say, you know, this week is going to be different, you're going to just come home and have a sensible piece of toast or maybe a small bowl of soup and go straight to bed. But then that one night rolls around, usually when the week is just stretching out ahead of me and the numbers from the day are still swimming in my head, and I just cave. It's incredibly frustrating because it's been this exact same pattern, at least that one night a week, every single week, for three whole months now. I just sit there the next morning at my desk feeling so drained and disappointed in myself, but I just can't seem to break the habit no matter how much I lecture myself in the rearview mirror on the way to work.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports weekly episodes of overeating followed by self-induced vomiting, occurring for at least three months. This meets the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2), which requires recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors, occurring at least once a week for three months. Binge-Eating Disorder (F50.81) is ruled out due to the presence of regular compensatory behaviors.
